subject: Availability covenant & monthly credit structure — Payden initial negotiation
messages:
From: Eleanor Shaw <elaine@payden.tech>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service availability covenant & credits — initial ask

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Payden is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Procurement/IT asked me to kick off the availability discussion so we can align on baseline commitments for the SOW. High-level asks from our side: 

- Baseline uptime: target 99.99% for production API endpoints (we will call these "critical endpoints").
- Monthly remedy: formula that pays service credits by minutes of unavailability; we typically cap credits at 25% of monthly subscription for a single month.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 200ms for normal traffic patterns.
- Scheduled maintenance: allowed but must be limited and with advance notice; we'll need a carve-in/exception definition.

I attached Payden_SOW_requirements.pdf to show expected traffic patterns and peak-hours. Can Redwood share a starting SLA template and a simple monthly credit calc so we can iterate?

Happy to hop on a call — procurement is available Tue/Wed.

Best,
Eleanor Shaw
Senior Procurement Manager
Payden Tech

Attachment: Payden_SOW_requirements.pdf (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Shaw <elaine@payden.tech>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service availability covenant & credits — initial ask

Eleanor — thanks for the clear deck and for the fast follow.

Quick response and a starting point from Redwood:

- Baseline uptime we propose: 99.95% monthly for the standard hosted API. For customers with reserved capacity we can discuss 99.97–99.99% depending on commitment level.
- Remedy calculation: standard monthly credit = (Downtime minutes / Total minutes in month) * Monthly service fee, with a monthly cap by default of 20% of the monthly fee.
- Latency: we can commit to 95th pctl < 250ms for multi-tenant hosted plans; dedicated pools/Private deployments can get tighter 95th pctl targets (sub-200ms).
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance with >=72h notice will be carveouts; emergency maintenance limited to specific operational incidents.

I'm attaching Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf with language and the default credit table. Laura (cc) will help with contract wording and compute the credit examples.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Tue 2025-06-10 10:00am PT to work through the credit math and carveouts. Does that work?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (stub)

From: procurement@payden.tech <procurement@payden.tech>

Cc: Payden Legal <legal@payden.tech>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service availability covenant & credits — Payden comments

Kimberly/Laura —

We reviewed the draft and Eleanor asked me to consolidate Payden's redlines. High level:

1) Baseline uptime: we are asking for 99.99% specifically for the set of critical endpoints used for payment and account sync. If Redwood needs to differentiate between endpoint classes we can accept a tiered approach, but critical endpoints must be 99.99.

2) Credits cap: 25% monthly cap is our starting position. Payden prefers not to have a hard 20% cap.

3) Latency: 95th pctl < 200ms for production traffic; we will provide sample traces to validate.

4) Maintenance carveouts: 48–72h notice window acceptable, but we will ask for blackout windows during Payden nightly processing (0200–0500 PT).

5) Remedy timing: credits should be applied to the next invoice within 30 days; we do not want to require a separate claims process.

I've attached a Payden redline (link below) and our procurement playbook sections for remedy. We need an updated draft with these points called out and the credit math shown for a representative monthly spend.

Thanks,
Marketa (Procurement) on behalf of Payden
procurement@payden.tech

Attachment: (internal redline link) https://payden.share/redline_payden_sla.pdf (external link stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@payden.tech <procurement@payden.tech>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service availability covenant & credits — Redwood counterproposal

Team — looping in legal ops and contracts on our side. Noting Payden's asks and proposing a middle path that keeps commercial risk manageable for Redwood while addressing Payden's priorities: 

- Tiered uptime: 99.97% for "core API set" (payment/account endpoints) + 99.95% for general endpoints. We'll include a concise appendix that enumerates the core API endpoints.
- Monthly credit cap: propose 20% cap by default, with flexibility to increase to 25% for a committed Dedicated deployment or a 12‑month minimum spend/top‑tier commitment.
- Latency: commit to 95th pctl < 220ms for hosted multi-tenant; provide a runbook and 14‑day sample traces for validation. For Dedicated/Private we can push to <200ms post-deployment tuning.
- Maintenance windows: propose scheduled maint carveout with >=48h notice; however, blackout windows (0200–0500 PT) can be marked as "no scheduled maintenance" for the first 90 days of the integration.
- Credits application: we will auto-apply credits to the next invoice for straightforward incidents — exceptions where investigation is required might need a short review. We will not put an onerous claims process in place.

I've attached a short spreadsheet that shows monthly credit examples for three spend bands. If Payden is ok with the tiered uptime + 20% standard cap (or 25% with minimum commitment), we can prepare a redline for Payden Legal.

Attachment: monthly_credit_calc.xlsx (stub)

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Service availability covenant & credits — Redwood counterproposal & next steps

Eleanor / Payden team — thanks for the clear feedback and Marketa for consolidating. To summarize Redwood's counterproposal and suggested path forward so legal can start drafting: 

1) Uptime: Tiered approach — 99.97% for enumerated core endpoints (we will send an appendix listing those) and 99.95% for the remainder. Dedicated deployments can be quoted to 99.99% with an annual committed capacity agreement.

2) Credits: Standard monthly cap 20% of the monthly fee, with an option to increase to 25% if Payden signs a 12‑month minimum committed plan or purchases a Dedicated pool. Credit formula will be automatic and applied to the next invoice for clear-cut downtime events.

3) Latency: For hosted multi-tenant we commit to 95th pctl < 220ms; dedicated/private deployments to be tuned to <200ms. We will provide 14 days of sample traces and a performance runbook.

4) Maintenance & blackout windows: scheduled maintenance carveouts with >=48h notice; no scheduled maintenance in Payden's blackout window (0200–0500 PT) for the first 90 days post-integration. Emergency maintenance remains carveout subject to incident classification.

5) Operational steps: Laura will produce a redline that reflects the above and include the core-endpoint appendix. Kimberly will schedule a 30-minute working session with Payden Legal + Procurement to walk the redline. Proposed meeting: Tue 2025-06-10 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent).

If these points generally align with Payden's expectations, please confirm and we will have legal/ops prepare the redline and a DocuSign-ready SLA addendum. If you'd like a temporary uplift in uptime for a pilot period we can scope that in pricing.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
